action: Customers: be wary of calls, emails or messages asking for passwords, codes or payments; iFood says it never asks for them and recommends two-step verification. Delivery workers: iFood says payout accounts need not be changed.
date_note: Date of the intrusion as stated by iFood, relayed by Olhar Digital and Tecnoblog; iFood confirmed it publicly on 19 November.
exec: iFood, a major Brazilian delivery platform, says personal details of customers, delivery workers and restaurant representatives were accessed; it has not said how many people.
plain: iFood says attackers accessed contact and registration details of some customers, delivery workers and restaurant contacts. It says passwords and cards were not accessed.

key_findings: iFood confirmed in a statement that a hacker attack exposed registration data of customers, delivery workers and partner restaurant representatives.

iFood Beneficios customers: only phone numbers; restaurant representatives: registered phone and/or CPF; delivery workers: name, email, phone and CPF per Tecnoblog and Canaltech (Olhar Digital also lists address), in some cases also agency and account numbers used for payouts.
iFood says passwords, cards, balances, statements and biometric data were not accessed and it found no evidence of disclosure or misuse so far; it notified the ANPD.

Canaltech: iFood sofre ataque hacker e expõe dados de clientes e entregadores

summary: iFood confirmed, per Olhar Digital, Tecnoblog and Canaltech, that attackers accessed its systems on 14 November. Exposed data varies: phone numbers for iFood Beneficios customers, phone and/or CPF for restaurant representatives, and for delivery workers name, email, phone and CPF (Olhar Digital also lists address), sometimes payout bank details. iFood says passwords and cards were not accessed, notified the ANPD and gave no count of people affected.
title: iFood confirms hacker attack exposed data of customers, delivery workers and restaurant representatives

validation.note: Olhar Digital, Tecnoblog and Canaltech (all 19 November) report iFood's own statement; the statement page itself was not read. Tecnoblog and Canaltech list delivery-worker data without address; only Olhar Digital lists address. Canaltech: iFood had not said how many people were affected. Follow-up 22 November found no later iFood or ANPD statement.

review.note: Compared with Olhar Digital and Tecnoblog: 14 Nov date, data per group, payout agency/account numbers, passwords/cards not accessed, no count, ANPD, advice
